Messages.Body:
Banishment
Type: Political Action
Choose a younger ready vampire. Successful referendum means that the chosen vampire is moved to the uncontrolled region (breaking any temporary control effects). The vampire is uncontrolled. Any cards and counters on that vampire stay with him or her (but they are out of play as long as the vampire remains uncontrolled).

From card rulings:
Temporary control effects are ended if the vampire is Banished, as normal, so the vampire would be placed in his previous (permanent) controller's uncontrolled region.

I think answers is clear but we have strange scenario today in game. So if you Banishment stolen vampire him going in his previous (permanent) controller's uncontrolled region,but if this controler is ousted then Banishment vampire is remowed from game,right?

Messages.Author: Hakuron
Messages.Body:
The original scenario and order of actions would be helpful to give the answer on what exactly happens in which order.

But in the end it is: The methuselah who stole the vampire will not keep it (permanently).
For example as soon as the stolen vampire is banished it returns to its owners uncontrolled region.

Messages.Author: beslin igor

scenario: player A stole vampire X from player B with Chameleon or Graverobing(example).
player C play Banishment on vampire X.
1) where vampire X going?
2) if player B is ousted where then vampire X going?
3) Ankha what is diferent in case stolen temporarily or permanently

Messages.Author: Yomyael
Messages.Body:
1) Vampire is going to the uncontrolled region of Player B, since Banishment only breaks temporary control effects. (see www.vekn.net/history-of-vtes-rules/443-rules-team-rulings-1-may-2000)
2) Since B was either the controller, or the vampire was in B's uncontrolled region, the vampire is removed from the game.
3) See 1) above. The only difference is, that Banishment breaks a temporary controll effect and therefore the vampire is returned to A's uncontrolled region.

edit: corrected answer later (I hope rightfully so)

Prince of Bonn, Germany

Messages.Author: Yomyael
Messages.Body:
Errr.... I had a total Brainfart when reading the question, somehow I assumed that Player B was the one stealing the vampire. I suspect Ankha made the same mistake when marking my answer as correct.

As far as I can tell, you are correct Kilrauko. In case 1) the vampire should go to Player A's uncontrolled region, since Player A is the permanent controller of the vampire. This would be in accordance to the quoted RTR. In case 2) nothing happens with the vampire, since the controller of the vampire is not ousted. In case 3) a vampire temporarily stolen by A is returned to B's uncontrolled region after a banishment. Should player B already have been ousted at that point, the vampire is removed from the game instead (as it would have been when the temporary controll effect would have expired).

I'm terribly sorry for the confusion!

Prince of Bonn, Germany

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> beslin wrote:
> So if you play Banishment on a stolen vampire, he goes to his previous (permanent) controller's uncontrolled region
>
Yes if the vampire was stolen temporarily (eg. Temptation)
Otherwise, he goes to his new permanent controller's uncontrolled region (eg. Form of Corruption).
>
> beslin wrote:
> ,but if this controler is ousted then Banishment vampire is remowed from game,right?
>
If the vampire is in the uncontrolled region of the player who is ousted, then the vampire is removed from the game. See above to determine in which uncontrolled region the vampire is.

> beslin wrote:
> scenario: player A stole vampire X from player B with Chameleon or Graverobing(example).
> player C play Banishment on vampire X.
> 1) where vampire X going?
>
A controls the vampire X permanently. The vampire goes to A's uncontrolled region.

> beslin wrote:
> 2) if player B is ousted where then vampire X going?
>
Nowhere since X is not controlled by B.
